text:
Alex T: Seeing a recurring Xid 61/ECC event on node gpu-cc-17 during nightly jobs. Passed the 3h soak yesterday but failed twice in the last 12h.
Mira P: Ugh, same node showed a single memory ECC correctable spike earlier. Any pattern (model, batch size, slot)?
Alex T: Both failures from large-generation jobs (seq len ~4096), batch 8. Logs attached to the job run.
Sanjeev R: Can you paste the dmesg snippet? Also run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,PERF` and `nvidia-bug-report.sh` to grab state.
Alex T: Copied dmesg excerpt:
```
[  345.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00:00): 61, PID=4123: GPC0WarpException
[  345.123457] NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: Xid 61, pid=4123, tid=0, Ch 00000001, GPC 0
[  345.123460] NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: Xid 61: Queues 0x000000ff, Host 0x00000000
```
Mira P: That Xid 61 often points at illegal memory access or ECC uncorrectable depending on driver. What driver/kernel?
Alex T: Ubuntu 22.04, nvidia-driver 525.85.05, kernel 5.15.0-80-generic.
Sanjeev R: Ok. Quick triage plan: 1) Quiesce node (drain), 2) Run targeted burn-in with both memory and compute stress for longer window, 3) Run vendor stress suite + collect hw telemetry, 4) If it reproduces -> RMA; if it stays green -> longer quarantine and monitor. Thoughts?
Mira P: Add step: reproduce at same seq len/batch and with small toy reproducer to isolate model vs runtime. Use `--seed` deterministic run.
QA Bot: Recommended commands: `kubectl drain gpu-cc-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then run `gpu-burnin --duration 6h --memtest --compute --log-level debug` and `stress-ng --gpu 4 --timeout 2h` as cross-check.
Alex T: Draining now. ops-bot please mark node OOS.
ops-bot: Marked node gpu-cc-17 as OOS (out of service) by request of Alex T. Annotated: Xid61/ECC spike.
Sanjeev R: While drained, attach PMEM and PCI metrics: `nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 1` and `ipmitool sdr list` for voltage/temps every 30s. We should capture ECC counters before/after: `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC`
Ruth (HW): If the burn-in reproduces Xid 61 within 6h, collect full `nvidia-bug-report.sh` and the `/var/log/kern.log`. Vendor will want timestamps and the bug report. Also include thermal camera if available.
Mira P: Quick note: last time a node passed our 3h soak then failed later, the issue only triggered under continuous small-batch workloads. I suggest we run a mixed workload panel: (1) big batch gen, (2) tiny-batch infer loop, (3) transformer pruning job. Rotate every 15m for 8h.
Alex T: Starting burn-in variant: `./scripts/gpu_burn_variant.sh --node gpu-cc-17 --duration 8h --mix big,tiny,prune --collect nvidia,ipmi,trace`
Sanjeev R: If the burn-in is clean, we should still keep node in quarantine and put it through a staged return: reenter pool at reduced capacity (1/4) and run canary traffic for 48h. If errors reappear -> RMA.
Alex T: Noted. Will post results here.
QA Bot: Checklist for post-run report: 1) total ECC correctable/uncorrectable deltas, 2) Xid occurrences with pids, 3) thermal/voltage anomalies, 4) reproducible step and command, 5) attached bug report tarball.
Alex T: Early update after 90m: memtest showed a single correctable ECC increment, Xid not yet reproduced. dmon logs attached to /tmp/gpu-cc-17-dmon.log
Mira P: Keep an eye on ambient datacenter temps — we had a chiller hiccup yesterday. Even small delta can affect flaky cards.
Ruth (HW): If ambient >28C, escalate to facilities; some wafers are sensitive to borderline temps.
Sanjeev R: If we can't repro in 8h, plan B is to swap PCI riser / power cable and repeat — flaky connectors have caused similar fingerprints.
Alex T: Makes sense. Scheduling a riser swap tomorrow if clean. Will update at completion (1762346022). :thumbsup:
